name: Red teaming
summary: azure-ai-evaluation RedTeam: attacker/scorer are Microsoft-managed; only the TARGET model accepts BYOM.
description: The Azure AI Evaluation `RedTeam` target can name the model under test as `{connection}/{deployment}`. This routes adversarial probe generation against a BYOM-backed target so users can red-team a gateway-hosted model deployment.
notes:
The `RedTeam` orchestrator accepts a BYOM-prefixed `azure_deployment` at construction, but the underlying PyRit `OpenAIChatTarget` cannot authenticate against the BYOM target so no adversarial prompt actually reaches the model. See `test.py`.

> Live scan on 2026-07-16 against `ai-foundry-3swd46vd3j22a` / connection `apim-3swd46vd3j22a-openai-s-for-ai-project-3swd46vd3j22a-1`: every attack turn returned `401 - {'statusCode': 401, 'message': 'Unauthorized. Access token is missing, invalid, audience is incorrect (https://ai.azure.com), or have expired.'}`. `final_results.json` reports `Attack Success: 0/0 attacks were successful` because PyRit never got a single prompt through.

Blocker is in PyRit's Foundry target: it hits `{project}/openai/v1` with an `https://ai.azure.com` audience, but the Foundry data plane wants `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default` for that path when BYOM-prefixed deployments are used. Until the eval SDK / PyRit target fix the audience or Foundry routes both, red-teaming against BYOM targets is unusable.
